chapter_title: Rotational Motion and Rigid Body Dynamics

topics.title: Moment of Inertia, Radius of Gyration, and Axis Theorems

subtopics.title: Moment of Inertia of Discrete Point Masses
subtopics.description: Definition I = sum(m_i r_i^2); rotational analogue of mass; dependency on choice of rotation axis.

subtopics.title: Moment of Inertia of Continuous Bodies via Integration
subtopics.description: Integral definition I = int r^2 dm; evaluation for thin rod (L^2/12), circular ring (R^2), uniform disc (R^2/2), hollow cylinder, solid cylinder, hollow sphere (2/3 R^2), and solid sphere (2/5 R^2).

subtopics.title: Parallel Axis Theorem (Steiner's Theorem)
subtopics.description: Theorem I = I_cm + M d^2; strictly requires one centroidal axis passing through center of mass.

subtopics.title: Perpendicular Axis Theorem for Planar Laminas
subtopics.description: Theorem I_z = I_x + I_y for planar two-dimensional lamina lying in xy-plane; misuse warning for 3D bodies.

subtopics.title: Radius of Gyration
subtopics.description: Definition k = sqrt(I / M) and geometric interpretation of mass distribution distance.

subtopics.title: Definition and Physical Meaning of Torque
subtopics.description: Vector cross product tau = r x F; moment arm r_perp; couples and origin independence for net zero force systems.

subtopics.title: Kinematics of Fixed-Axis Rotation
subtopics.description: Angular kinematics under constant angular acceleration alpha: omega = omega_0 + alpha t, theta = omega_0 t + 1/2 alpha t^2, omega^2 = omega_0^2 + 2 alpha theta.

subtopics.title: Fundamental Equation of Rotational Dynamics
subtopics.description: Dynamic relation tau_net = I alpha; application to rigid bodies rotating about fixed inertial axes; Atwood machines with massive pulleys.

subtopics.title: Rotational Work, Kinetic Energy, and Power
subtopics.description: Rotational kinetic energy K_rot = 1/2 I omega^2; rotational work dW = tau dtheta; work-energy theorem for rotational systems W_net = Delta K_rot; rotational power P = tau omega.

topics.title: Angular Momentum of Particles and Rigid Bodies

subtopics.title: Angular Momentum of a Single Particle
subtopics.description: Vector definition L = r x p = m (r x v); reference point dependence; straight line motion with nonzero impact parameter.

subtopics.title: Transformation of Angular Momentum to External Reference Points
subtopics.description: Decomposition L_O = L_cm + r_cm x P_total for composite systems and general planar motion.

subtopics.title: Angular Momentum of a Rigid Body about Fixed Axis
subtopics.description: Scalar and vector relation L = I omega along principal axis of symmetry.

subtopics.title: Universal Principle of Conservation of Angular Momentum
subtopics.description: Torque-momentum theorem tau_net,ext = dL/dt; constancy of L when tau_net,ext = 0; isolated systems and central force fields.

subtopics.title: Rotational Systems with Internal Mass Reconfiguration
subtopics.description: Conservation I_i omega_i = I_f omega_f; non-conservation of rotational kinetic energy during internal configuration shifts.

topics.title: Rolling Motion, Friction Interaction, and Toppling

subtopics.title: Kinematic Constraint of Pure Rolling
subtopics.description: No-slipping condition v_cm = R omega, a_cm = R alpha; instantaneous center of rotation (ICR); cycloidal trajectory of rim points.

subtopics.title: Dynamics of Pure Rolling on Horizontal Surfaces
subtopics.description: Static friction as an adjustable constraint force; zero friction condition; forward versus backward static friction depending on line of action of external force.

subtopics.title: Rolling Motion on an Inclined Plane
subtopics.description: Acceleration down incline a = g sin(theta) / (1 + I_cm/(M R^2)); minimum friction coefficient mu_min = tan(theta) / (1 + M R^2/I_cm); total mechanical energy conservation.

subtopics.title: Conditions for Sliding versus Toppling of Rigid Blocks
subtopics.description: Critical horizontal force F_crit = M g b / (2 h); normal reaction migration to edge; critical incline angle tan(theta) = b / h.

explicit_exclusions.rationale: Gyroscopic precession, full 3D inertia tensors, and asymmetric top rotation are designated as Olympiad-tier extensions in kb/taxonomy/syllabus.yaml and excluded from core JEE Advanced narrative.

explicit_exclusions.topic: Planetary Orbits and Central Field Keplerian Potentials
explicit_exclusions.rationale: While conservation of angular momentum explains Kepler's Second Law, the detailed gravitational potentials and celestial mechanics belong to Chapter 7: Gravitation.

explicit_exclusions.topic: Pure Translational Collisions without Angular Impulses
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Point particle collisions belong to Chapter 5: Center of Mass and Linear Momentum.
